value.comment: The briefing record. Its columns are cintel:Briefing's own data properties (direct_properties_only), so the class is the whole of what a briefing record can hold. The projection is jet_rules/clinical_intel/briefing_projection.jr and it is an allowlist, so exclude_properties here is a belt on top of a brace rather than the control. TWO ENCODINGS AS OF 2026-09-09: the same entity map, two renderers, and the exclusion list is the only thing that differs between what the model sees and what the template sees - which is what a controlled pair needs, and what stops there being a second extraction path to keep in step. A second entry could not have been added while provenance_schema_name was set: entityColumnOf refuses a channel spec encoding more than one column, because which of them the prompt was built from is a question the operator cannot answer (jets/compute_pipes/infer_provenance.go). Retiring the schema is what lifts that, so the two edits are ONE edit and this file is where both land. Measured rather than read: with a schema named the same pair of encodings is refused naming both columns, and with none it resolves to no check at all.
value.name: Briefing

column_encodings.comment: The prompt. Ten exclusions in three groups. THREE are structural - jets:key, rdf:type and jets:source_period_sequence carry nothing a briefing is about. TWO are the ones that are not a belt, and they are the ones naming a cintel: property: cintel:Briefing_Member_ID and cintel:Briefing_Disclaimer both have to be ON the record and out of the prompt, and a denylist is the only way to say so - EncodeColumnData has no include_properties. FIVE are new on 2026-09-09 and are the pharmacy node's. hc:Drug_Name, cintel:Maintenance, cintel:Fill_Count and cintel:Fill_Date are the components cintel:Medication concatenates: the prompt must carry ONE value per medication, because the briefing flattens across pharmacy events and two multi-valued properties on one node are two independent sets - a member on two drugs, one maintenance and one not, could be described with the pair crossed. The components stay on the entity for the template arm, which wants four values rather than a sentence to parse, and extractAsEntity applies exclude_properties at every depth of its recursion so a property can be on the entity and out of the prompt. cintel:Adherence is the fifth and it is a duplicate rather than a component: the four BP_Medication rules partition on whether adherenceText exists and adherenceText exists exactly when cintel:Adherence does, so the ratio is inside cintel:Medication on every node that carries it and the bare property is a second rendering of one number - `Adherence: 0` beside a joined value that already says `adherence 0.00`. Excluding it withholds nothing from the model and removes what the minimum-necessary rule is about. What it costs is precision: cintel:Medication renders the ratio at two decimals and the bare property is unrounded, which matters to nothing that reads a briefing and is worth saying rather than leaving to be discovered. ENCODING SWITCHED FROM toon TO json ON 2026-09-10. TOON was chosen for compactness and nothing had tested what it cost. Measured over the same 22 members with the same fact set, one entity map encoded both ways and both arms scored against that same object: JSON is better on FIVE of nine categories and TOON on one. Maintenance misstatements fall 18 to 10, conditions omitted 26 to 16, untrue statements 13 to 9, adherence attributed to a drug carrying none 13 to 6. TOON wins advisory language, 1 of 22 against 6, which is real and does not offset five in the other direction. What TOON buys is 2.8 percent of the prompt - 30,394 tokens against 31,255, 861 tokens over 22 records. THE WHOLE DIFFERENCE LIVES IN THE EXPANDED STRATUM: where a record's lists carry multi-valued fields or mixed key sets the two encodings diverge eightfold on maintenance, and where they serialise tabular they are equivalent - and the saving is 4.5 percent where it costs nothing and 1.2 percent where it costs a great deal. The mechanism is unexplained: the expanded form is the LESS compact and MORE redundant of the two, which is not the direction a compactness argument predicts. Not a claim that TOON is worse in general - one model at 3B, 22 curated members, one run.

The deterministic briefing (jets/agentic/briefing/prose). It is the CONTROL rather than a second product: no model result is reported without it, and the two arms differ in the renderer and in nothing else. remove_model_prefixes is true because prose.Render refuses a map whose keys still carry a prefix, by name - a briefing rendered off prefixed keys would come out empty and read as a member with no claims. cintel:Briefing_Disclaimer is NOT excluded here and is excluded from the prompt, which is the difference that matters most: Render refuses a briefing carrying no notice, because the artefact is notice, rule, prose in that order and prose delivered without its notice is the one output worse than no output. The four medication components are not excluded either - the renderer reads the drug name, the indicator, the count and the dates rather than parsing them back out of cintel:Medication, which would encode join_values' separator in a second place. Nor is cintel:Adherence, and the renderer deliberately prints nothing from it: the ratio's observation window ends at the last fill, so a member who STOPS filling scores higher than one who does not, and what replaces it is what the ratio is computed from - the fill count and the most recent fill date.

THE THREE EXCLUSIONS BELOW ARE STRUCTURAL AND ARE A DEPARTURE FROM THE DESIGN, WHICH SAYS AN EMPTY SET. Two reasons, and the first was measured rather than reasoned about. isEntity is `has at least one outgoing triple` and RdfSession.FindS unions the META graph with the asserted and inferred ones, so in a real rule session the class resource named by rdf:type IS an entity and extractAsEntity RECURSES INTO IT - measured by giving cintel:Briefing two triples and encoding the same fixture both ways: with an empty set the entity map gains `type: {type: owl:Class, base_class: {type: owl:Class}}` and grows, with these three it does not. Against a real meta graph that is a walk into the class model on every record. The prose is byte-identical either way, because Render ignores the key; what it costs is work per record and a trap for the next renderer. Second, and this is why the departure makes the controlled comparison STRONGER rather than weaker: these same three are excluded from the prompt column, so they are not a difference between the arms at all. With them the two lists differ in exactly the six content properties the template needs and the prompt must not repeat; with an empty set they would differ in nine, three of which are not content.

THE THREE EXCLUSIONS BELOW ARE STRUCTURAL AND ARE A DEPARTURE FROM THE DESIGN, WHICH SAYS AN EMPTY SET. Two reasons, and the first was measured rather than reasoned about. isEntity is `has at least one outgoing triple` and RdfSession.FindS unions the META graph with the asserted and inferred ones, so in a real rule session the class resource named by rdf:type IS an entity and extractAsEntity RECURSES INTO IT - measured by giving cintel:Briefing two triples and encoding the same fixture both ways: with an empty set the entity map gains `type: {type: owl:Class, base_class: {type: owl:Class}}` and grows, with these three it does not. Against a real meta graph that is a walk into the class model on every record. The prose is byte-identical either way, because Render ignores the key; what it costs is work per record and a trap for the next renderer. Second, and this is why the departure makes the controlled comparison STRONGER rather than weaker: these same three are excluded from the prompt column, so they are not a difference between the arms at all. With them the two lists differ in exactly the six content properties the template needs and the prompt must not repeat; with an empty set they would differ in nine, three of which are not content.

value.comment:
THE OPTIMIZER STATISTICS PROCESS (2026-10-24). It counts what the clinical rules' sessions hold, so that the rule compiler can order each rule's antecedents by the rows they add, and puts the counts into this workspace as this process's own file, jet_rules/Optimizer_Statistics.optimizer_statistics.json (jetstore#2368). It is Patient_Profile's rule run (the same three source objects, sharding, sort, merge and rule session over jet_rules/clinical_intel/cintel_main.jr) with optimizer_statistics set on the jetrules step, and with only the care-management record kept: no briefing, so no model is called.

HOW THE FILE GETS INTO THE WORKSPACE. Each node of the rule step writes a partial file, counts summed over its sessions, to <stage>/process_name=Optimizer_Statistics/session_id=<session>/optimizer_statistics/. The process's report (reports/config.json, Optimizer_Statistics) calls the run_reports function merge_optimizer_statistics, shipped with JetStore, which merges the partials exactly into jetstore/workspaces/jets_ws/jet_rules/Optimizer_Statistics.optimizer_statistics.json, and touches no other statistics file; updateLookupTables then syncs that file into the workspace and records it as an override, as a lookup a report writes is. IT TAKES EFFECT AT THE WORKSPACE'S NEXT COMPILE, NOT WHEN THE REPORT ENDS: this process runs on cpipesNativeSM, whose reports run in the run_reports Lambda, which does not compile (SkipCompileWorkspace). So compile once from the UI after a run, or let a later deployment's start-up compile apply the override; the Fargate reportsSM route would compile. The compiler reads the file from JetStore with jetstore#2361, and every process's own file from jetstore#2368. Nothing in the statistics is a data value: every key is a predicate or a constant of a rule's antecedent.

RUN IT ON DEMAND, NOT WITH EVERY PRODUCTION RUN. A new file changes the compiled network, so it is regenerated when the workspace owner decides the data's shape has moved, not on every run. The order changes no result.

THE FILE IS A WORKSPACE OVERRIDE, AND A DEPLOYMENT TREATS IT AS ONE. From JetStore 4.0.4 the start-up compile that applies an override compiles under a fresh version, so the pipelines fetch the workspace with the file. On a stack before 4.0.4 it stamps the image's JETS_VERSION and the pipelines read the image's compiled workspace without the file: compile once from the UI after such a deployment, or commit the file. Only the rule order is at stake, never the results.

ERROR REPORTING IS BUILT IN HERE AND IS NO LONGER WIRED BY HAND (2026-09-11). This document used to carry two instances of the four coordinated edits that feature exists to retire - an error_channel on the jetrules operator and one on the infer operator, a channels entry declaring each one's nine columns, an output_tables entry binding each to jetsapi.process_errors, and a whole further pipe reading each error channel and map_record-ing it into the table writer. All eight are gone and nothing replaces them in this file. SynthesizeDefaultErrorChannels gives every operator that reports row-level failures a channel of its own, fans them into one sink and adds the single table writer, at startup, after the conditional transformation specs have been applied and before anything validates or prunes (SynthesizeDefaultErrorChannels, jets/compute_pipes/error_channel_default.go:179). What the node receives is an ordinary configuration it cannot tell from the one this file used to spell out - and it carries THREE COLUMNS THE HAND-WRITTEN SPECS NEVER WROTE: cpipes_step_id, error_channel and operator_type are on DefaultProcessErrorColumns and were not on the nine this document declared, so a triage query over jetsapi.process_errors gets values here that it got NULLs for before.

THIS REVERSES A DECISION THIS FILE STATED, AND THE COST IS EXACTLY ONE THING. The infer step's error_channel carried the argument for being explicit, and it is reproduced rather than deleted: the synthesis only fills a NIL channel, JETS_DEFAULT_ERROR_REPORTING=false turns the synthesis off wholesale, and therefore an error channel a deployment switch can remove is one nobody notices the absence of. That argument is not wrong and it is not withdrawn - it is priced. What setting it aside costs is this and nothing else: IN A DEPLOYMENT THAT SETS JETS_DEFAULT_ERROR_REPORTING=false, THE JETRULES STEP AND THE INFER STEP OF THIS PIPELINE STOP REPORTING ROW-LEVEL FAILURES, and the run still succeeds. JETS_DEFAULT_ERROR_MAX_COUNT lowers what error reporting costs without that consequence and is what a deployment wanting less error data should reach for first. Nothing else moves: the channel names and the table entry are the synthesis's rather than this document's, both bind jetsapi.process_errors, and no consumer of that table distinguishes a synthesised row from a hand-wired one. THE DAY SOMEBODY SETS THAT VARIABLE, THIS PARAGRAPH IS WHAT THEY FIND, which is the whole of what the removed declaration was protecting.

WHY THE TRADE IS WORTH TAKING HERE RATHER THAN IN GENERAL. This document is about to acquire a sibling - patient_profile_template.pc.json, the same pipeline with a render operator where this one has infer - and what makes the pair a controlled comparison is that the two differ in the operator block and in nothing else. Eight hand-wired error-reporting elements duplicated across two documents are eight ways for that to stop being true, and they are the part of the document that says least about what the pipeline does. A reader wanting the four edits back does not have to invent them: this comment names all four, and git history holds them verbatim.

channels.comment: The briefing record. Its columns are cintel:Briefing's own data properties (direct_properties_only), so the class is the whole of what a briefing record can hold. The projection is jet_rules/clinical_intel/briefing_projection.jr and it is an allowlist, so exclude_properties here is a belt on top of a brace rather than the control. TWO ENCODINGS AS OF 2026-09-09: the same entity map, two renderers, and the exclusion list is the only thing that differs between what the model sees and what the template sees - which is what a controlled pair needs, and what stops there being a second extraction path to keep in step. A second entry could not have been added while provenance_schema_name was set: entityColumnOf refuses a channel spec encoding more than one column, because which of them the prompt was built from is a question the operator cannot answer (jets/compute_pipes/infer_provenance.go). Retiring the schema is what lifts that, so the two edits are ONE edit and this file is where both land. Measured rather than read: with a schema named the same pair of encodings is refused naming both columns, and with none it resolves to no check at all.

column_encodings.comment: The prompt. Ten exclusions in three groups. THREE are structural - jets:key, rdf:type and jets:source_period_sequence carry nothing a briefing is about. TWO are the ones that are not a belt, and they are the ones naming a cintel: property: cintel:Briefing_Member_ID and cintel:Briefing_Disclaimer both have to be ON the record and out of the prompt, and a denylist is the only way to say so - EncodeColumnData has no include_properties. The components stay on the entity for the template arm, which wants four values rather than a sentence to parse, and extractAsEntity applies exclude_properties at every depth of its recursion so a property can be on the entity and out of the prompt. cintel:Adherence is the fifth and it is a duplicate rather than a component: the four BP_Medication rules partition on whether adherenceText exists and adherenceText exists exactly when cintel:Adherence does, so the ratio is inside cintel:Medication on every node that carries it and the bare property is a second rendering of one number - `Adherence: 0` beside a joined value that already says `adherence 0.00`. Excluding it withholds nothing from the model and removes what the minimum-necessary rule is about. What it costs is precision: cintel:Medication renders the ratio at two decimals and the bare property is unrounded, which matters to nothing that reads a briefing and is worth saying rather than leaving to be discovered. Measured over the same 22 members with the same fact set, one entity map encoded both ways and both arms scored against that same object: JSON is better on FIVE of nine categories and TOON on one. Maintenance misstatements fall 18 to 10, conditions omitted 26 to 16, untrue statements 13 to 9, adherence attributed to a drug carrying none 13 to 6. TOON wins advisory language, 1 of 22 against 6, which is real and does not offset five in the other direction. What TOON buys is 2.8 percent of the prompt - 30,394 tokens against 31,255, 861 tokens over 22 records. THE WHOLE DIFFERENCE LIVES IN THE EXPANDED STRATUM: where a record's lists carry multi-valued fields or mixed key sets the two encodings diverge eightfold on maintenance, and where they serialise tabular they are equivalent - and the saving is 4.5 percent where it costs nothing and 1.2 percent where it costs a great deal. The mechanism is unexplained: the expanded form is the LESS compact and MORE redundant of the two, which is not the direction a compactness argument predicts. Not a claim that TOON is worse in general - one model at 3B, 22 curated members, one run.

The deterministic briefing (jets/agentic/briefing/prose). It is the CONTROL rather than a second product: no model result is reported without it, and the two arms differ in the renderer and in nothing else. remove_model_prefixes is true because prose.Render refuses a map whose keys still carry a prefix, by name - a briefing rendered off prefixed keys would come out empty and read as a member with no claims. cintel:Briefing_Disclaimer is NOT excluded here and is excluded from the prompt, which is the difference that matters most: Render refuses a briefing carrying no notice, because the artefact is notice, rule, prose in that order and prose delivered without its notice is the one output worse than no output. Against a real meta graph that is a walk into the class model on every record. The prose is byte-identical either way, because Render ignores the key; what it costs is work per record and a trap for the next renderer. With them the two lists differ in exactly the six content properties the template needs and the prompt must not repeat; with an empty set they would differ in nine, three of which are not content.

prompt_templates.comment:
THE BRIEFING IS PROSE AS OF 2026-09-09. It was a schema of short bounded fields; the model is now asked for a paragraph and the infer step below names no provenance schema, so nothing constrains the decoding and nothing checks the answer. Read this comment for what the prompt no longer says as much as for what it does - the argument for each removal is why the removals are not losses.

WHAT WENT. The json-object instruction went with the response_format it described: there is no schema to match. The four copy-verbatim bullets went with the fields they were about - a diagnosis copied whole, a drug name and its indicator copied from the fills - because prose has no fields to copy into and the check that made copying verifiable is retired with them. The empty-list instruction went the same way. What the earlier prompt was doing with those bullets was making the answer GROUNDABLE by making it a selection; the finding is that an output optimised for groundability converges on its source, and at the limit the output is the source, so the selection is a rule session's work and is now done by briefing_projection.jr.

WHAT STAYED, AND EACH FOR A STATED REASON. The audience sentence stays: it is the only statement anywhere of who reads this, and the read-aloud posture is the reordering fact of the use case. The TOON-list sentence stays: a header written `Diagnosis[3]: A,B,C` is still three values and a model that reads it as one still writes a fused diagnosis - the field is gone, the misreading is not. The no-invention paragraph stays and is now about facts rather than about values in named fields, and it names what may not be inferred as well as what may not be added, because prose is where an inference fits and a bounded field was not. The advisory prohibition stays and is the ONE guardrail that still has a subject: the advisory lexicon is a lexical scan needing no path, and an advisory sentence found under a prompt that forbade it is a finding while one found under a prompt that said nothing is an artefact.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT. It does NOT enumerate the four elements the design decided - volume and window, last encounter, conditions, medications with fill recency - and that is the decision most likely to be read as an oversight. Enumerating them would make the model arm a restatement of the template's specification, and the open question is whether a model adds anything a template does not: a prompt that dictates the template's content answers that question by construction. It says NOTHING about the adherence ratio either. The design says to read the model's treatment of it as a datum on that question rather than to design it out - an unasked-for adherence judgement delivered to a non-clinician is the failure the design's guardrails are written around, so a model that volunteers one has answered the question rather than malfunctioned. The ratio reaches the prompt inside cintel:Medication; the bare cintel:Adherence property does not, and the Briefing channel's comment says why that withholds nothing.

HISTORY WORTH KEEPING, because it is why several sentences read as they do. The TOON-list and count sentences were added 2026-09-06 after a live vLLM run copied `Diagnosis_Code[3]: H6690,Z23,Z00129` into one field eight times and counted condition groups rather than events; ollama had not needed them. The illustration that once stood in the no-invention rule was a real-looking diagnosis, "(B182) Chronic viral hepatitis C", and on 2026-09-06 the model copied it into the answer for two members whose summaries never mention it - the example read as content, and a prompt that must forbid invention should not contain an inventable value. Nothing here is illustrated for that reason. The counting and date instructions went on 2026-09-09: BP_BriefingCounts10 and BP_BriefingDates10 compute the two counts and the two dates in briefing_projection.jr, so they are lines of the claim summary this prompt renders rather than a question asked of a 3B model.

AND IT STILL CARRIES NO response_format, for a new reason. Until today the one copy lived in provenance/patient_briefing.pv.json and the operator adopted it through provenance_schema_name. The operator names no schema now, so nothing is adopted and the field being absent here is what leaves the model unconstrained - which is what asking for prose means.
prompt_templates.system_prompt:
You prepare briefings for a call-centre representative who is about to speak with a member. The representative is not a clinician and takes no clinical action.

Write a short briefing in prose - about 100 words, no headings and no lists. Answer with the briefing and nothing else.

The claim summary is TOON. A field written as `Diagnosis[3]: A,B,C` is a list of three separate values, not one value containing commas.

Every fact you write must come from the claim summary you are given. Do not add a condition, a medication, a date or a count that is not in the summary, and do not infer a diagnosis, a severity or a cause from what is there.

The briefing is informational. Do not recommend, advise or instruct.

pipes_config.comment: The rule step, and the one that produces both the care-management record and the briefing entity. ITS error_channel WAS REMOVED ON 2026-09-11 WITH THE REST OF THE HAND WIRING. It named process_errors.out, and process_errors was a channel declaration, an output_tables entry and a further map_record pipe in this file - four edits for one operator. SynthesizeDefaultErrorChannels now gives this operator its own channel at startup, with the three triage columns the hand-written spec did not carry. What that costs, and it is a real cost rather than a tidy-up, is stated at the head of this file: a deployment setting JETS_DEFAULT_ERROR_REPORTING=false silently stops reporting row-level failures for this step.
The care-management record, written without ever having been sent to a model.

The briefing, and it is PROSE again as of 2026-09-09. It is worth being exact about what that does and does not restore, because this step has now been prose, then fielded, then prose, and the third state is not the first.

THE FIRST PROSE STEP was three paragraphs mapped from raw_response onto cintel:Profile_Prose, guarded by the sentence "Never infer diagnoses not present in the data" in a system prompt - the design's two guardrails both absent, each in the way the design warns about. The model was handed a serialised copy of cintel:Patient_Profile, which inherits hc:Member, so the member's name, date of birth and address were in the prompt.

THE FIELDED STEP replaced it with a schema of short bounded fields over a minimum-necessary projection, checked against the input entity by jets/agentic/briefing rather than trusted.

THIS STEP keeps the projection and drops the schema. What makes it not a return to the first is that the prompt is built from cintel:Briefing rather than from the profile - the direct identifiers are not in it and cannot be, since the projection is an allowlist - and that the fact set the model renders is a rule-engine product rather than a claim summary the model has to select from. The guarantee is CONSTRUCTION rather than checking: a call that is shown only the briefing entity cannot assert a source fact it was never shown. That is a weaker guarantee than the fielded step's and a stronger one than the first step's, and saying which is the whole of what this task delivered.

WHAT IS LOST WITH provenance_schema_name, stated here rather than left to be discovered. The provenance checker's Field is a selector into the briefing (jets/agentic/briefing/schema.go), and grounded, count_of and within_span all compare values at paths; a paragraph has no paths. So all seven provenance rules retire with the structured response they checked, the last three with this edit, and nothing automated reads the model's answer any more (what replaces them is still to be decided). Confine returns nil on a schema declaring no response_format, so nothing mechanically requires a briefing schema to declare the notice field either. THE NOTICE CANNOT GO MISSING: BP_Disclaimer10 asserts it on every briefing with no premise beyond the briefing existing, and no model is involved. What is lost is the check and not the field, and the case it would have caught is a future briefing schema written without one.

cintel:Briefing_Document still carries the answer verbatim. The reason has changed rather than the mapping: it used to be the checked unit, because an array cannot be a column value and is re-encoded as a json string on the way into one (applyMappings, jets/compute_pipes/pipe_transformation_infer.go), so a check over the mapped columns would have seen one opaque leaf. Now it is simply where a paragraph goes. Nothing reads it but a reader.

AND THE ARM IT IS MEASURED AGAINST IS IN THIS FILE. cintel:Briefing_Prose is a second column_encodings entry on the Briefing channel, written by the jetrules step above from the same entity map with an empty exclusion list. Every record therefore carries both briefings and they differ in the renderer and in nothing else, which is why no model figure from this pipeline is reported without its control.

infer_config.comment:
Runs against whichever inference server the deployment is running, and says so once. backend reads $INFER_BACKEND, which shardingInitializeCpipes copies from the process environment and the reducing path replays out of cpipes_startup_json, so every step of one run agrees even if the service is redeployed mid-run; unset means ollama, which is what this step was before the key existed. ResolveInferBackend rewrites this into a type: ollama or type: vllm operator before anything else sees it, so the executors, the error-channel synthesis and the validator keep seeing the two operators they already knew and no dispatch site learned a third. Everything but the specialized keys is shared rather than duplicated, because InferCommonSpec is one embedded struct on both backends rather than two parallel lists - that is what makes this a single block instead of a conditional_config carrying a second copy of output_mapping and error_channel. think is ollama's and is inert on vLLM, which logs it at resolution rather than refusing it, since refusing it is what would make a two-backend document impossible. structured_output is deliberately absent and as of 2026-09-09 it is INERT rather than a choice: the vllm operator's default is json_schema since jetstore#2101, the arm that actually constrains on the pinned v0.28.0 image, and naming it here would pin a version-dependent choice in a workspace file - but vllmRequestBase reads config.ResponseFormat and there is none now, since retiring provenance_schema_name removed the only copy this operator was adopting one from. The same holds of ollama's format. Both backends therefore issue an UNCONSTRAINED request, which is what asking for prose means and is a change of kind rather than of degree: the encoding experiment and the backend benchmark are no longer comparing two constrained decoders, and the earlier findings said in terms that both arms carrying the same schema was what made a converged result readable. This paragraph is kept rather than deleted with the constraint it describes, because the day a briefing wants a shape again is the day the version-dependent argument matters, and a deleted paragraph is a decision somebody makes twice. model is one string because the deployed vLLM serves granite4.1:3b under that id; a deployment serving it under another name would need a split here and does not have one. It was pinned to the literal "vllm" on 2026-09-06 while the deployment could not answer: the operator read $INFER_BACKEND and the CDK never gave that variable to the sharding starter lambda, so every step resolved to ollama and called /api/* on a vLLM server. jetstore#2108 plumbed it and the reference is back, which is the point of the field - the deployment says which server is running and this document does not. A local run needs INFER_BACKEND in the environment the driver inherits; unset still means ollama. Four mappings left on 2026-09-09 and their columns did not. cintel:Medical_Event_Count, cintel:Pharmacy_Event_Count, cintel:Earliest_Service_Date and cintel:Latest_Service_Date are still declared on cintel:Briefing and are still columns of the Briefing channel - they are asserted by BP_BriefingCounts10 and BP_BriefingDates10 in the rule session, so they are already on the record this operator receives. The infer operator augments its input record in place (validateInferChannels requires the input and output channels to share a channel spec for exactly that reason), so a column it does not map is a column it does not touch. Two things follow that a mapping could not give: the four values are in the prompt, because they are properties of the entity the Briefing channel serialises into cintel:Briefing_Input; and they survive the model, because a record whose inference failed still carries them. required: true on the two counts used to mean 'fail the record if the model omitted the count' - it now means nothing to omit.

AND IT NOW SETS SAMPLING PARAMETERS, WHICH IT DID NOT UNTIL 2026-09-10. Until today this step sent model, stream and messages and nothing else - the operator sends no sampling parameters unless the config supplies options - so the server sampled at its own default and 0 of 22 briefings repeated between two runs over identical data. temperature 0 is set FOR A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN FOR A PRODUCT: one experiment compares two encodings and another two backends, and a sampled decoder puts variance into the cell that is not the variable under test. Nothing about a briefing itself argues for greedy decoding, so a deployment measuring something else may want another value and should say here why.

THE SEED IS NOT REDUNDANT BESIDE temperature 0 IN PRINCIPLE, AND IT IS NOT WHAT MAKES THIS ARM REPRODUCIBLE - both halves measured 2026-09-10 rather than argued. Greedy decoding is deterministic given identical logits and logits are not identical under continuous batching, so a seed is the parameter that covers what temperature 0 does not. What the measurement says, over the real 18,108-character M007 briefing prompt against the deployed vLLM serving granite4.1:3b: ten sequential calls give 10 distinct completions with no options and 1 with temperature 0, with or without the seed, and that still holds with a different member's call between each pair. At pool_size 4, each call batched against three different members, the same two arms give 5 distinct of 16 and 4 of 16 - so the seed does not repair batch-composition nondeterminism and neither does greedy. THE SEED IS READ RATHER THAN IGNORED: at temperature 1 seed 42 and seed 7 each yield one distinct completion in six and the two differ, while no seed yields six. It is kept because it costs nothing and because it is what makes a nonzero-temperature deployment reproducible, NOT because it was observed to help here. THE RESIDUE IS A POOL SIZE RATHER THAN AN OPTION: an encoding or backend accuracy cell is one draw only at pool_size 1, and at pool_size 4 it has to be repeated with the count stated.

WHERE THE TWO KEYS LAND DIFFERS BY BACKEND AND THE BLOCK IS THE SAME EITHER WAY, which is what a step naming backend $INFER_BACKEND needs. vLLM merges options into the request body at the TOP LEVEL, because that is the OpenAI api's shape rather than a choice (vllmRequestBase, jets/compute_pipes/pipe_transformation_vllm.go:413), and refuses at build time any key the operator sets itself (vllmReservedRequestKeys, jets/compute_pipes/pipe_transformation_vllm.go:85) - neither temperature nor seed is reserved. ollama nests them under options, which is ollama's own shape (BuildRequest, jets/compute_pipes/pipe_transformation_ollama.go:124). InferCommonSpec carries NO Options field, so this key is not a promoted one: it is InferSpec's own (InferSpec, jets/compute_pipes/pipes_model.go:1648) and resolveInferSpec copies it onto whichever backend spec it builds (resolveInferSpec, jets/compute_pipes/resolve_infer_backend.go:74). One block therefore serves both backends, and that was read off the request body each backend's BuildRequest produced rather than off the struct tags. A NOTE FOR WHOEVER ADDS A KEY HERE: this vLLM accepts unknown request fields rather than rejecting them, so a misspelt parameter is silently inert and a call that succeeds is no evidence that its options were honoured.

THE error_channel THAT USED TO SIT BESIDE output_mapping IS GONE AS OF 2026-09-11, AND ITS ARGUMENT IS NOT. It read that SynthesizeDefaultErrorChannels only fills a NIL channel and that JETS_DEFAULT_ERROR_REPORTING=false turns the synthesis off wholesale, so an error channel a deployment switch can remove is one nobody notices the absence of. That is still true. It is now the STATED COST of the removal rather than a reason against it, and the comment at the head of this file is where it is stated, together with what this document gains by not carrying eight hand-wired error-reporting elements its sibling would have to carry too. What travels this step's synthesised channel is what travelled the declared one - call failures and mapping failures, provenance findings having retired with provenance_schema_name - plus the three triage columns the hand-written spec never wrote.

description: Complete configuration for a Compute Pipes pipeline

value.comment:
THE TEMPLATE ARM OF A CONTROLLED PAIR (2026-09-11). This document is patient_profile.pc.json with a render step where that one has an infer step. Everything else about the two pipelines is the same run: the same three source objects, the same sharding, the same sort, the same rule session over jet_rules/clinical_intel/cintel_main.jr, the same two output channels off it, the same care-management record written without a model, and the same briefing writer. What differs is who writes cintel:Briefing_Document - a 3B model in v1, a configured text template here - and the pair exists so that the difference between two briefings is attributable to that and to nothing else.

WHAT THIS DOCUMENT IS FOR, SAID ONCE RATHER THAN INFERRED FROM THE DIFF. An earlier measurement found the template arm more accurate than the model arm on this briefing (22 of 22 against 17 of 18 member-runs carrying a maintenance misstatement), and it measured it through a renderer written in Go and reached through a column encoding. This pair makes the renderer a configured document and gives it an operator, so the template arm becomes a PIPELINE rather than an encoding - which is what makes it deployable, and what makes the comparison between the two arms a comparison between two things a deployment can actually choose. THIS DOCUMENT CLAIMS NOTHING ABOUT WHICH ARM IS BETTER. It measures nothing, and two files shipping side by side is not a recommendation.

THE DIFFERENCE IS THE OPERATOR AND THE TWO THINGS THE OPERATOR NAMES, WHICH IS NARROWER THAN THE REQUIREMENT ASKS FOR AND IS NOT THE SAME SENTENCE. The requirement reads 'v1 and v2 differ in the operator block and in nothing else'. Three blocks differ, and the second and third are not slack:
  1. THE OPERATOR. type infer with infer_config becomes type render with render_config, on the same input channel Briefing.source, writing the same output channel Briefing.out.
  2. THE TEMPLATE DECLARATION THE OPERATOR NAMES. prompt_templates carries the one thing v1's operator names - the prompt - and text_templates carries the one thing this operator names - the briefing document. Each pipeline declares its own operator's template and neither declares the other's. Keeping v1's prompt_templates here would leave a prompt for a model this pipeline does not call, and an inert key is what the earlier InferSpec is this repository's worked example of the cost of.
  3. THE PROJECTION THE OPERATOR READS. cintel:Briefing_Input excludes ten properties in v1 and three here. This is the one a reader should stop at, and the paragraph below is why it could not be avoided.
A fourth block differs and has no declared behaviour behind it: the comment on the cintel:Briefing_Prose column_encodings entry carries one added paragraph saying what that column is in a pipeline with no model in it. Every field of that entry is byte-identical to v1's and must stay so.

THE TWO OPERATORS CANNOT READ THE SAME PROJECTION, AND THIS WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN REASONED ABOUT. The design argues that the render operator and the infer operator have the same input contract - one channel, one column, one serialised entity - and that is true of the CONTRACT and false of the CONTENT. v1's cintel:Briefing_Input is a minimum-necessary projection built for a model, and five of the ten properties it withholds are properties the template reads: cintel:Briefing_Disclaimer, hc:Drug_Name, cintel:Maintenance, cintel:Fill_Count and cintel:Fill_Date. Rendering patient_profile_briefing against v1's projection produces THREE violations on the reference fixture - one on the notice, one per pharmacy event on the drug name - and the artefact that comes out has no notice and reads 'Medications: .'. Under on_error pass_through that is a record with no briefing on it, every record, silently. So the exclusion list had to change, and what it changes to is not invented: it is the list cintel:Briefing_Prose already carries, the three structural properties, which is the same entity map the deterministic renderer has been reading.

WHY THAT DOES NOT WEAKEN THE PAIR. The controlled pair's rule is that the two arms differ in the renderer and in nothing else, and its mechanism was two column_encodings entries on one channel differing only in their exclusion list - one for what the model sees, one for what the template sees. That mechanism is unchanged; what moved is where the two lists live. In v1 they are two columns of one document; across the pair they are one column of two documents. The entity is the same entity, walked by the same extractAsEntity from the same rule session, and the exclusion list is still the only thing that differs between what the model reads and what the template reads. A reader who wants the two side by side in one run still has it: cintel:Briefing_Prose is on the Briefing channel of BOTH documents and is unchanged in either.

AND THAT MAKES THIS PIPELINE SELF-CHECKING. Whether entity_encoding briefing_prose retires now that the operator ships was left open, with the recommendation to keep it for now and decide once the operator has run and the comparison is cheap. It is kept, and the comparison is cheaper than that: every record this pipeline writes carries cintel:Briefing_Prose, rendered inside the jetrules column encoder from the RDF walk, and cintel:Briefing_Document, rendered by the operator from a json document decoded back out of a column. THE TWO ARE THE SAME ARTEFACT BY TWO CODE PATHS AND THEY SHOULD BE BYTE-IDENTICAL. A Go test asserts that over seventeen fixtures; this asserts it on real members, and a disagreement between the two columns of one record is a defect with nowhere to hide. That is the argument for keeping the encoding for now and it is also the argument for retiring it afterwards: a second path that agrees on every record has finished proving what it was kept to prove.

ERROR REPORTING IS BUILT IN HERE, as it is in v1 and for the same reasons - see that document's head comment, which is the one place the argument is written out. SynthesizeDefaultErrorChannels gives the jetrules step and the render step a channel each, fans them into one sink and adds the table writer, at startup. The cost is the same and it is the same sentence: a deployment setting JETS_DEFAULT_ERROR_REPORTING=false stops reporting row-level failures for both steps and the run still succeeds. That matters marginally more here than there, because a render violation is the only way this pipeline can fail a record and it is silent under the default on_error.

IT IS REGISTERED AND THEREFORE RUNNABLE. process_config key 50105, process_name Patient_Profile_Template, in process_config/base__workspace_init_db.sql beside v1's 50101. A .pc.json with no process_config row is inert, and an inert document is one nobody finds out is broken - which is this repository's own note about this exact trap. Registering it does not schedule it: a pipeline runs when somebody starts it, and the row is what makes starting it possible.

channels.comment: The care-management view. It no longer carries a serialised copy of itself: cintel:Claim_Summary encoded the whole entity, and cintel:Patient_Profile inherits hc:Member, so the member's name, date of birth and address were in the prompt. The minimum-necessary projection is the Briefing channel below.
channels.name: Patient_Profile

channels.comment: The briefing record. Its columns are cintel:Briefing's own data properties (direct_properties_only), so the class is the whole of what a briefing record can hold. The projection is jet_rules/clinical_intel/briefing_projection.jr and it is an allowlist, so exclude_properties here is a belt on top of a brace rather than the control. TWO ENCODINGS AS OF 2026-09-09: the same entity map, two renderers, and the exclusion list is the only thing that differs between what the model sees and what the template sees - which is what a controlled pair needs, and what stops there being a second extraction path to keep in step. A second entry could not have been added while provenance_schema_name was set: entityColumnOf refuses a channel spec encoding more than one column, because which of them the prompt was built from is a question the operator cannot answer (jets/compute_pipes/infer_provenance.go). Retiring the schema is what lifts that, so the two edits are ONE edit and this file is where both land. Measured rather than read: with a schema named the same pair of encodings is refused naming both columns, and with none it resolves to no check at all.
channels.name: Briefing

column_encodings.comment:
The template's input, and it is v1's prompt column with a different exclusion list. THREE EXCLUSIONS RATHER THAN TEN, AND THE SEVEN THAT WENT ARE THE WHOLE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THIS PIPELINE AND ITS SIBLING BESIDE THE OPERATOR ITSELF (2026-09-11). The three that stay are the structural ones - jets:key, rdf:type and jets:source_period_sequence carry nothing a briefing is about, and the second of them is not a belt: isEntity is 'has at least one outgoing triple' and RdfSession.FindS unions the META graph, so with an empty set extractAsEntity recurses into the class model on every record. That measurement is reproduced here rather than re-argued; the Briefing_Prose entry below carries the long form.

WHY THE OTHER SEVEN COULD NOT STAY, MEASURED RATHER THAN REASONED ABOUT. Five of them are properties the template reads: cintel:Briefing_Disclaimer, hc:Drug_Name, cintel:Maintenance, cintel:Fill_Count and cintel:Fill_Date. Rendering patient_profile_briefing against v1's ten-exclusion projection produces three violations on the reference fixture - the notice's require, and one per pharmacy event on the drug name - and what the engine emits is an artefact with no notice whose medication paragraph reads 'Medications: .'. The remaining two, cintel:Briefing_Member_ID and cintel:Adherence, are not read by the template and are not excluded either, because the list this one adopts is cintel:Briefing_Prose's and adopting it wholesale is what makes the two columns of this record the same entity map. cintel:Adherence in particular is DELIBERATELY not rendered by the template - the ratio's observation window ends at the last fill, so a member who stops filling scores higher than one who does not - and a property the renderer ignores costs nothing on the entity.

THE COLUMN KEEPS ITS NAME AND THE NAME IS STILL TRUE. cintel:Briefing_Input is the serialised entity the briefing step reads. In v1 the briefing step is a model and the projection is minimum-necessary because the minimum-necessary rule says what a model may be shown; here the briefing step is a renderer running inside the pipeline, shown nothing that leaves it, and the minimum-necessary rule has no subject. Renaming the column in one of the two documents would have made the pair harder to read for no gain and would have cost a data model change that v1 would then carry an empty column for.

THE ENCODING IS json AND THE OPERATOR IS TOLD SO TWICE ON PURPOSE. The render step below sets input_encoding json as well, which resolveRenderInputEncoding treats as an override it must agree with - a disagreement between the two is a BUILD failure rather than a per-record decode failure, because both are constants of the configuration. Stating it twice is normally what that function's own doc block argues against, and it is done here for one reason: an earlier report of this column said toon, which was true until the encoding was switched on 2026-09-10 after measuring JSON better on five of nine categories and TOON better on one, for 2.8 percent of the prompt. A document that states its own encoding is one the next reader cannot misremember, and the build failure is what makes stating it safe rather than duplicative.

IN THIS DOCUMENT IT IS NOT A CONTROL AGAINST A MODEL, IT IS THE SECOND PATH TO THE SAME ARTEFACT (2026-09-11). The render step below writes the same briefing into cintel:Briefing_Document from a decoded json document, and this entry writes it into cintel:Briefing_Prose from the RDF walk inside the column encoder. The two are the same renderer reached two ways and they should agree byte for byte on every record, which is the Go test's assertion made on real members rather than on seventeen fixtures - see the head comment, and the open question of retiring this entry, which this arrangement exists to answer. EVERY FIELD OF THIS ENTRY IS BYTE-IDENTICAL TO patient_profile.pc.json's AND MUST STAY SO: the exclusion list, the encoding and remove_model_prefixes are what make the two documents comparable, and a drift here would be a difference between the pipelines that nobody is looking for. The rest of this comment is that document's, verbatim; its sentences about the model arm are about the sibling pipeline and read as such.

The deterministic briefing (jets/agentic/briefing/prose). It is the CONTROL rather than a second product: no model result is reported without it, and the two arms differ in the renderer and in nothing else. remove_model_prefixes is true because prose.Render refuses a map whose keys still carry a prefix, by name - a briefing rendered off prefixed keys would come out empty and read as a member with no claims. cintel:Briefing_Disclaimer is NOT excluded here and is excluded from the prompt, which is the difference that matters most: Render refuses a briefing carrying no notice, because the artefact is notice, rule, prose in that order and prose delivered without its notice is the one output worse than no output. The four medication components are not excluded either - the renderer reads the drug name, the indicator, the count and the dates rather than parsing them back out of cintel:Medication, which would encode join_values' separator in a second place. Nor is cintel:Adherence, and the renderer deliberately prints nothing from it: the ratio's observation window ends at the last fill, so a member who STOPS filling scores higher than one who does not, and what replaces it is what the ratio is computed from - the fill count and the most recent fill date.

THE THREE EXCLUSIONS BELOW ARE STRUCTURAL AND ARE A DEPARTURE FROM THE DESIGN, WHICH SAYS AN EMPTY SET. Two reasons, and the first was measured rather than reasoned about. isEntity is `has at least one outgoing triple` and RdfSession.FindS unions the META graph with the asserted and inferred ones, so in a real rule session the class resource named by rdf:type IS an entity and extractAsEntity RECURSES INTO IT - measured by giving cintel:Briefing two triples and encoding the same fixture both ways: with an empty set the entity map gains `type: {type: owl:Class, base_class: {type: owl:Class}}` and grows, with these three it does not. Against a real meta graph that is a walk into the class model on every record. The prose is byte-identical either way, because Render ignores the key; what it costs is work per record and a trap for the next renderer. Second, and this is why the departure makes the controlled comparison STRONGER rather than weaker: these same three are excluded from the prompt column, so they are not a difference between the arms at all. With them the two lists differ in exactly the six content properties the template needs and the prompt must not repeat; with an empty set they would differ in nine, three of which are not content.

text_templates.comment: The patient_profile briefing, as a text template document. It is what jets/agentic/briefing/prose renders, expressed in the text template notation, and jets/agentic/template is the engine that reads it. This file is the ONE copy: it is inlined into patient_profile_template.pc.json's text_templates array and TestTheShippedPipelineCarriesThisDocument compares the two. Every element below carries the argument for its predicate, because a predicate is a line of logic and the code it reproduces has a comment where this has none.

elements.comment: The notice, and the engine has no idea what it is. By design, two of Render's three refusals become assertions in the document and one leaves the engine. This is the first of the two. The require fires on blank rendered text and not only on an absent property, which is what prose.Render does - it compares the trimmed disclaimer with the empty string - so a whitespace-only notice is refused here as it is there.
elements.text: {{Briefing_Disclaimer require 'the briefing entity carries no Briefing_Disclaimer; the notice is asserted unconditionally by BP_Disclaimer10 and the rendered artefact is notice, rule, prose in that order'}}

elements.comment: The rule, which is 68 hyphens verbatim from prose.go and is inside width, so it is never wrapped. A literal paragraph: the second of the two most briefing-shaped things in the artefact, and the notation needed no concept for either.

The body, and the fallback is this group's rather than the document's. prose.Render puts the notice and the rule ABOVE the empty sentence, so a briefing with no activity is notice, rule, sentence rather than sentence alone; a flat element list cannot express that, because the notice always emits and a document-level fallback would never fire.
elements.empty: No claims activity on record for this member.

elements.comment: renderBody reaches the empty sentence by two predicates that are not equivalent, and this nested group is the first of them: both counts zero is an early return BEFORE any element runs, so it suppresses the conditions element too. The specification writes it as a conjunct on the conditions element alone, which is wrong for the medications element - a Pharmacy_Event_Count of 0 beside a populated event list and no medical activity emits Medications: there and the empty sentence in the code. A group is the honest shape: the guard is written once, it covers all three elements, and the outer group's empty still fires because a group that emits nothing leaves its parent with no emitting child. The second predicate - every element produced nothing - is the outer group's empty, so both are kept and neither is a special case. The two count[] disjuncts are countOf's fallback: see the medical element below.
elements.when: Medical_Event_Count > 0 or (Medical_Event_Count == '' and has_Briefing_Medical_Events[]|count > 0) or Pharmacy_Event_Count > 0 or (Pharmacy_Event_Count == '' and has_Briefing_Pharmacy_Events[]|count > 0)

elements.comment: Elements 1 and 2 of the briefing in one paragraph: how much and how recently, then what the last contact was. Three decisions are transcribed rather than invented. latest_by is applied to the EVENTS and not to Latest_Service_Date, because the briefing-level extremum is a date and this clause needs the encounter it belongs to. The care setting is verbatim in a labelled clause and is not folded into a fluent sentence, because the article rule produces at a telehealth over the 52 place-of-service descriptions. And with supplies the guard that the original sketch forgot: a span scoped to a chain yielding nothing emits nothing, so the sketch's Most recent contact: , 5 May. cannot happen. The two Medical_Event_Count branches are decided here rather than inherited: countOf prefers the projected count and falls back to the length of the list it counts, and dropping the fallback does not cost a sentence - it makes a member with events and no count render No claims activity on record, which is an affirmative false statement and is the failure mode the prefixed-entity refusal exists to prevent. The reproduction is exact for an absent or blank count and not for one present and non-numeric, which needs a negation the notation does not have.
elements.text: {{if Medical_Event_Count != ''}}{{Medical_Event_Count|words|sentence}} medical {{Medical_Event_Count|plural: 'visit'}}{{end}}{{if Medical_Event_Count == ''}}{{has_Briefing_Medical_Events[]|count|words|sentence}} medical {{has_Briefing_Medical_Events[]|count|plural: 'visit'}}{{end}} on record{{if Earliest_Service_Date|d_MMMM != '' and Latest_Service_Date|d_MMMM_yyyy != ''}}, between {{Earliest_Service_Date|d_MMMM}} and {{Latest_Service_Date|d_MMMM_yyyy}}{{end}}. {{with has_Briefing_Medical_Events[]|latest_by: Service_Date}}Most recent contact: {{if Care_Setting != ''}}{{Care_Setting}}, {{end}}{{Service_Date|d_MMMM}}.{{end}}

elements.comment: Element 3, and it is third rather than first on purpose: a briefing that opens with a diagnosis list reads like a clinical handover, and under the read-aloud test the first line is the line most likely to be spoken. Do not improve the order. The parenthesised code is stripped in the prose and stays on the entity - it exists so a checker can match a whole string exactly, and it is noise to a member. The gate is the rendered list rather than count > 0, because elementConditions filters values that are empty AFTER the code is stripped and only then asks whether anything is left: a Condition_Summary of one blank string gives count 1 and would emit Conditions on record: with nothing after it. join skips an empty item here, so the gate and the text are the same chain and there is no rule about what precedes the join.

Element 4, the one element a representative can act on with no judgement at all. It reads the components and never the joined Medication value, which is the second of Render's assertions moved into the document: recovering the drug name from the joined value would encode join_values' separator in a second place. The gate is the LIST and not Pharmacy_Event_Count, because elementMedications returns early only when the count is not positive AND the list is empty, so guarding on the count would emit Medications: . for a count with no list. Maintenance is matched against both cases, which is decided here: strings.EqualFold over a trimmed value is true for y and for Y and for nothing else, so the disjunction is that function written out rather than an approximation of it, and the specification's case-sensitive == is left alone for Care_Setting's sake. The second Fill_Count branch is fillCount's fallback, as above: the projected count wins and the fill dates are the same fact counted rather than a different one. The individual fill dates are not listed - the count and the latest carry the whole of what this element does, and three dates per drug is length for a member on four maintenance drugs.
elements.text: Medications: {{each has_Briefing_Pharmacy_Events[] sep: '; ' last: '; and '}}{{Drug_Name require 'a pharmacy event of the briefing carries no Drug_Name; the renderer reads the components of a medication and never the joined Medication value, so that the separator the rules join it with lives in one place'}}{{if Maintenance == 'Y' or Maintenance == 'y'}}, a maintenance medication{{end}}{{if Fill_Count != ''}}, {{Fill_Count|words}} {{Fill_Count|plural: 'fill'}}{{if Fill_Date[]|max|d_MMMM != ''}}, most recently {{Fill_Date[]|max|d_MMMM}}{{end}}{{end}}{{if Fill_Count == '' and Fill_Date[]|count > 0}}, {{Fill_Date[]|count|words}} {{Fill_Date[]|count|plural: 'fill'}}{{if Fill_Date[]|max|d_MMMM != ''}}, most recently {{Fill_Date[]|max|d_MMMM}}{{end}}{{end}}{{end}}.

pipes_config.comment: The rule step, and the one that produces both the care-management record and the briefing entity. ITS error_channel WAS REMOVED ON 2026-09-11 WITH THE REST OF THE HAND WIRING. It named process_errors.out, and process_errors was a channel declaration, an output_tables entry and a further map_record pipe in this file - four edits for one operator. SynthesizeDefaultErrorChannels now gives this operator its own channel at startup, with the three triage columns the hand-written spec did not carry. What that costs, and it is a real cost rather than a tidy-up, is stated at the head of this file: a deployment setting JETS_DEFAULT_ERROR_REPORTING=false silently stops reporting row-level failures for this step.
The care-management record, written without ever having been sent to a model.

The briefing, and in this document it is RENDERED rather than inferred (2026-09-11). patient_profile.pc.json's step of the same name carries a long account of how that briefing came to be prose - three paragraphs, then a schema of bounded fields, then prose again - and it is not reproduced here, because none of it is about this step. What is worth carrying across is the one sentence that is: the guarantee this artefact rests on is CONSTRUCTION rather than checking, and it is stronger here than there. v1's guarantee is that a model shown only the briefing entity cannot assert a source fact it was never shown. This step's guarantee is that a renderer reading a document cannot assert anything the document does not contain, because there is no generator - every sentence it emits is a span of a template the workspace declares, and every value in it is a path into the entity the rule session built.

WHAT THAT COSTS IS FLUENCY AND WHAT IT BUYS IS THE GUARDRAILS THE DESIGN ASKS FOR, THREE OF WHICH STOP BEING GUARDRAILS. The advisory prohibition, the no-invention rule and the copy-verbatim discipline are all rules a prompt has to state and a checker has to police when a model writes the briefing; a renderer cannot violate them, so there is nothing to state and nothing to police. What remains a real risk is the one this pipeline can still get wrong: a template that says something misleading says it on every record, which is a defect in a reviewed document rather than a drift in a sampled decoder, and is why the template is a workspace artefact with its argument beside each predicate.

AND THE ARM THIS IS MEASURED AGAINST IS IN THIS FILE TOO, WHICH IT WAS NOT IN v1. cintel:Briefing_Prose is written by the jetrules step above from the same entity map by a different code path - inside the column encoder, off the RDF walk, by jets/agentic/briefing/prose. Every record this pipeline writes therefore carries the same briefing twice and the two should be byte-identical. See the head comment for why that is a self-check rather than a redundancy.

render_config.comment:
WHAT IT DOES. It reads cintel:Briefing_Input, decodes it as a json document, renders the patient_profile_briefing document declared in text_templates above, and writes the result to cintel:Briefing_Document - the same column v1's model answer lands in, so a consumer of a briefing reads one column whichever pipeline produced it. The record is augmented in place, which is why the input and output channels share the Briefing channel spec: validateInferChannels enforces that for this operator exactly as it does for the infer operators, and a column the step does not write is a column it does not touch.

WHAT IT DOES NOT WRITE, AND THE ABSENCE IS INFORMATION. cintel:Briefing_Model_Name is left null. v1 maps model_name onto it and a briefing that carries one was produced by a model; a briefing that carries none was produced by this pipeline. Nothing had to be configured for that to be true, and it is worth saying because the alternative - writing the template's key into a column named for a model - would have made the two arms indistinguishable in the one field that tells them apart.

THERE IS NO template ALTERNATIVE TO template_name AND THAT IS A DESIGN DECISION RATHER THAN AN OMISSION. prompt_template sits beside prompt_template_name on the infer operators because a prompt is a string a step can reasonably carry inline; a template document is a nested structure, and inlining one in a transformation spec would put the whole notation inside a pipes_config step where no second step could share it. Whether the document should instead be a workspace file referenced by name was settled as inline at the configuration root by the user's instruction, and is recorded rather than dissolved - the day a template is shared by three pipelines is the day PromptTemplateSpec's own 'so a template can be shared by several steps and pipes' argument applies at the file level too.

on_error pass_through IS THE DEFAULT AND IS WRITTEN OUT, because what it means here is not what it means on a mapping operator. A render fails a record for two reasons: the input column does not decode to a document, or a require the template declares is not satisfied. The second is the one that matters - the notice's require - and it was settled that a violation fails the ROW rather than writing a partial artefact, on prose.Render's own argument that prose delivered without its notice is the one output worse than no output. pass_through then means the record continues with cintel:Briefing_Document unwritten: the member is still on the output, the briefing is not, and the failure is on the error channel with the member id beside it. drop would lose the record and fail would stop the run; neither is right for an artefact whose absence is recoverable by rerunning.

row_key_column IS SET AND v1's infer STEP DOES NOT SET IT. That is a difference inside the operator block and it is deliberate: the render operator reports ONE ERROR ROW PER VIOLATION rather than one per record, because a violation carries which item of an each it was about and collapsing them throws that away - so an error channel from this step can carry several rows for one member, and without a key nothing says they are one member's. cintel:Briefing_Member_ID is a data property of cintel:Briefing and therefore a column of this channel, and it is the identifier a triage query over jetsapi.process_errors would join on.

max_error_count IS LEFT AT ITS DEFAULT OF 20, WHICH IS A CHOICE THIS COMMENT OWES A READER. The corpus this pipeline has been measured over is 22 members and a template failure is systematic rather than per-record - a projection that withholds a property the template reads fails every record identically, which is exactly the defect measured above - so the first twenty rows carry the whole diagnosis and the cap is doing what it is for. A deployment over a real membership that wants the full count should raise it here rather than reach for JETS_DEFAULT_ERROR_MAX_COUNT, which governs the synthesis rather than this operator.

AND THERE IS NO error_channel BLOCK, for the reason v1 has none: SynthesizeDefaultErrorChannels gives this operator a channel of its own at startup, with the three triage columns a hand-written spec never carried, and reportsRowLevelFailures names the render operator alongside map_record, jetrules, ollama, embed and vllm. What travels it is the two row-level failures named above.

value.comment:
The demonstration corpus as a compute_pipes pipeline: a `generator` source that reads no file, one site operator wrapping the reviewed generator, and one partition writer per corpus output table.

**Two steps, and they run on two engines.** Step 0 is the sharding step and is **Go's**: `ShardFileKeys` refuses `input_channel.type == "generator"` in sharding mode by name, so a corpus generator can only live in a *reducing* step, and a reducing step needs a sharding step in front of it. Step 0's input channel is typed `input`, which the Python node does not declare, so `cpipes-node check` over **this whole document** exits 1 naming that token -- correctly. The Python node is never handed this document: a starter flattens one step into `pipes_config` and the node sees step 1 alone. The split is legal because `ecsOrLambdaChoice` sits after `runStartReducingTask`, which runs once per reducing iteration, so one pipeline may run one step on Go and another on Python.

**The trigger is a schema event, which is a `compute_pipes.SchemaProviderSpec`.** Its `format` is unmarshalled onto the `_main_input_` provider and decides the output format for every writer below -- CSV or Parquet, chosen at trigger time. Its `env` carries `$NBR_NODES` and `$NBR_ROWS`. It names the cohort spec and copies neither the cohort size nor the run seed, because both are authored on the cohort spec and a second spelling is the defect.

**Sizing.** `nbr_rows` is `ceil(total_households / nbr_nodes)`. Over the shipped demonstration tree the household total is **6,197 at the authored 10,000 members** (128 at 200, 250 at 400), so `nbr_rows` is 6197, 1550, 775, 155 or 16 at 1, 4, 8, 40 or 400 nodes. `nbr_nodes` is how much each node holds; `cluster_config.default_max_concurrency` is how many run at once, and the two are different numbers.

**Where the corpus lands, and what happens when nobody says.** The two cases were ruled apart on 2026-09-19. **Writing multipart files, the worker nodes write straight to the output folder** -- the folder is already shared, so staging the data and copying it afterwards is work nobody asked for. **Writing a single file, the workers write their partition to stage and one worker `merge_files` it into the output.** The shape is `anonymize_file.pc.json`'s, step `Anonymize Data`: a base `output_channel` and one `conditional_config` entry that replaces it.

**This document inverts the example's polarity, deliberately.** There, `stage` is the base and multipart is the override; here **multipart is the base and the single-file arm is the override**, taken when `${CORPUS_MULTIPART_OUTPUT}` is `'0'`. The argument is the asymmetry of saying nothing. With `stage` as the base, a deployment that sets no variable writes the **whole corpus into JetStore's stage prefix** -- scratch, outside the session-keyed output location and outside the S3 lifecycle policy the installation carries, which is written about the output prefix and is the only thing that ever removes a failed run's remains -- and then pays for **twelve single-node merge steps** it did not ask for. With multipart as the base, a deployment that sets no variable gets the corpus **in its session-keyed output location**, complete and readable; what it does not get is a *shape*, and a shape is cheaper to be wrong about than a location. The rejected reading is worth recording because it is a real argument: **one file per table is exactly the shape the corpus's QC harness reads**, so a stage default would hand a do-nothing deployment a corpus this project can already check. It is refused because **that question is open** -- whether a JetStore-written corpus is read as a directory of parts or as a directory of files is not yet ruled, and a default chosen to suit an unruled question is a ruling smuggled into a default.

**The guard's right-hand side is quoted and the example's is not, deliberately.** `parseValue` reads a literal's type off its spelling, so an unquoted `0` is a *number*; `opEqual` then coerces the left side with `String2Int`, and an **unset** variable is still the literal `${CORPUS_MULTIPART_OUTPUT}`, which is not an int -- so the guard **errors** rather than evaluating false, in Go and in the Python node alike (measured in both). `'0'` keeps both sides strings, so an unset variable compares unequal and the base arm is taken. **That is what makes this document's default reachable at all**, and it is a property `anonymize_file.pc.json` does not have: its multipart variable must be set there or the step's own guard raises.

**Three environment variables, and none of them has a default JetStore can supply.** `${CORPUS_OUTPUT_PATH}` is the key prefix under which a run's output lands; `$SESSIONID` is JetStore's own and is what keeps two runs apart; `${CORPUS_OUT_BUCKET}` is the destination bucket and `${CORPUS_MULTIPART_OUTPUT}` selects the arm. **A `context` entry cannot default any of them**: `collectEnvSettings` applies `context` *after* the schema event's `env`, so it would overwrite the trigger rather than fill in behind it -- the one key the engine defaults conditionally is `$DATE_FILE_KEY`, and it does it with an explicit nil test nothing else gets. **So `${CORPUS_OUT_BUCKET}` unset does not mean JetStore's bucket** -- it means a bucket literally named `${CORPUS_OUT_BUCKET}`. The engine's own spelling for *JetStore's bucket* is the sentinel string **`jetstore_bucket`**, which both the writer and the merge test by name, so a site that wants JetStore's own bucket sets `CORPUS_OUT_BUCKET=jetstore_bucket`.

**Two things the Python node once accepted and did not do, and now does.** This paragraph said otherwise until 2026-09-28, nine days after both were built, which is why it names them rather than dropping them. `stream_data_out` streams a part into the object store through `put_stream` and never holds it whole, as Go's arm at `s3_device_writter.go:40` does. A per-channel `bucket` is honoured: the destination is resolved as Go resolves it -- an empty value and the literal `jetstore_bucket` both meaning the node's own bucket -- and the writer holds a store bound to that bucket, so `${CORPUS_OUT_BUCKET}`, defaulted to `$INPUT_BUCKET` by the main-input provider, is the bucket the corpus lands in.

**What this document does not do.** It declares no `common_runtime_args`: that is the starter's, and authoring one here would be a second spelling of a derived fact. **It writes the corpus's own `run_manifest.json` beside the data, last** (ruled 2026-09-29): each node of `generate_corpus` writes a fragment under `run_manifest_nodes/` in its `done`, and the last step, `write_corpus_manifest`, assembles them and writes `${CORPUS_OUTPUT_PATH}/$SESSIONID/run_manifest.json` -- so the rule *a corpus is complete iff its manifest is present* holds at the folder a deployer is pointed at. JetStore's own manifest is still written to the stage prefix and says which outputs were written; the corpus's says what produced them. The two `adjudicated_claim` projections below stay on `stage` and are deliberately **not** governed by the output-folder rule: they are a QC pipeline's input, not corpus output, and promoting them to the output folder would put an intermediate where a consumer looks for the corpus's twelve tables.

cluster_config.comment: `default_max_concurrency` is how many nodes run at once and is not the partition count: `nbr_nodes` above decides how many partitions exist and therefore how much each node holds, and this decides wall-clock and cost.

schema_providers.comment:
**No `format`, deliberately**, on `anonymize_file.pc.json`'s precedent: the schema event supplies it, and it is what every output channel below takes its format and its `device_writer_type` from. Authoring one here would pin the corpus to one format and defeat the run-time format selection. A generator pipeline still needs this provider -- `envSettings` *is* its `env` (`actions_coordinate_cp.go:104`) and a node fails without it. The trigger file is written in the same format the event names, so the sharding step parses it with the same rule the writers encode with, and there is one fact rather than two.

**`env` here is a *default*, and it fills in behind the trigger rather than overriding it (measured 2026-09-22).** `shardingInitializeCpipes` finds this provider by `source_type` (`GetSchemaProviderConfigBySourceType`, `schema_providers.go:470`), and then unmarshals the schema event **onto it** (`actions_start_common.go:215`). Go's `json.Unmarshal` into a non-nil map reuses it and keeps existing entries, so a key the event names wins and a key it does not name survives -- and `prepareCpipesEnv` then uses this very map as `envSettings`, by reference (`actions_start_common.go:1918`). **So this is the fill-behind the request said does not exist.** The request said *no `context` entry can default it*, which is true and beside the point: the mechanism was never `context`, it was the provider the event is merged into, and nobody looked there.

**`${CORPUS_OUT_BUCKET}` defaults to `$INPUT_BUCKET`, so the corpus lands in the bucket its own trigger file came from.** A deployment that sets the variable overrides this; one that does not gets the input bucket instead of a bucket literally named `${CORPUS_OUT_BUCKET}`, which is what was asked for. **`$INPUT_BUCKET` is JetStore's own env key for exactly this** -- `prepareCpipesEnv` sets it from the main-input schema provider's `bucket` (`actions_start_common.go:1963`), which is the field `ListS3Objects` is handed when the sharding step reads the input (`actions_shard_file_keys.go:53`), so *the bucket the input came from* and *the bucket the output goes to* are one fact rather than two. **This document is the first in any workspace this repository pins to use it**, which is half the reason for choosing it over the `jetstore_bucket` sentinel: the two resolve to the same bucket for a trigger file JetStore wrote itself, and they differ the moment a client drops one in their own bucket.

**The indirection resolves, and it resolves in two passes.** `utils.ReplaceEnvVars` (`jets/utils/env_utils.go:15`) re-scans while a `$` remains, so `${CORPUS_OUT_BUCKET}` becomes `$INPUT_BUCKET` and then the bucket name; map iteration is random and the outer loop is what makes that order-independent, measured over five runs on 2026-09-22.

**It also satisfies the startup gate added 2026-09-21** (`ValidateResolvedBuckets`, `bucket_validation.go`), which refuses to start a run whose bucket still carries a `$`: the gate sees the resolved value, so with this default the corpus starts, and a site that sets `CORPUS_OUT_BUCKET` to something the environment does not supply is refused at startup rather than writing somewhere nobody looks.

**One thing to know about the path this default takes.** The two writers test the sentinel on the *raw* value and substitute afterwards -- `pipe_executor_merge_files.go:135` then `:142`, and `pipe_transformation_partition_writer.go:485` then `:492` -- so `${CORPUS_OUT_BUCKET}` passes the test as a non-sentinel and becomes `jetstore_bucket` in a variable called `externalBucket`. It does not leak: four sinks each test again (`s3_copy_file.go:50` and `:53`, `awsi.go:598`, `s3_device_worker.go:63`, `merge_files.go:165`). **The guarantee is held by the sinks rather than by construction**, which is recorded as an open JetStore issue.

**`nbr_rows_in_record` is here rather than on an input channel for the same reason `env` is**: the matrix marks it `applicable=no` on all four `InputChannelConfig` tokens and `applicable=yes` on `SchemaProviderSpec/default`, and `syncOutputChannelWithSchemaProvider` copies it onto every output channel that names this provider and sets none of its own.

The records are empty by construction and the operator reads none of them -- see the site step.
